sentences.text: The property falls in fully developed commercial area.
The notification for acquisition of 41 bighas of land issued on 12.06.1997 in Village Chandrawali.
Thereafter, various interested persons including the petitioner had filed their objections and claims before the concerned SDM and he was to held an inquiry in respect of amount of compensation.

The petitioner along-with other interested persons had also filed an application U/s 11, L.A. Act for fixing the date for inquiry.

( V ) ISSUE-WISE FINDINGS:-
ISSUE NO.1: "Whether the amount of compensation awarded to the petitioners is liable to be enhanced?
If so, at what rate?

OPP"
a) Onus to prove this issue is upon the petitioner.

By virtue of this reference, the petitioner is seeking enhancement in compensation in respect of compulsory acquisition of their Shop No.1/1142B and 1/1143, First Floor situated in Chandrawali @ Shahdara, Delhi measuring 23.95 square meters on account of acquired land beneath the shop, damages on account of change in place of business including business goodwill.

b) In support of this issue, the petitioner in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW7/A deposed that the petitioner is the owner of land underneath Shop no.1/1142 B and 1/1143, Railway Road, Shahdara, Delhi-110032.
The Ground Floor Shop was owned by Sh. Jawand Singh and Sh. Harcharan Singh.
The First Floor shop is owned by the petitioner and the second floor is owned by Sh. Raghubir Singh another son of Sh. Jawand Singh.
Accordingly, in the land underneath the shop measuring 23.95 sq. mtrs. was owned by Sh. Jawand Singh and Sh. Harcharan Singh to the extent of 1/3rd share.
The share of the petitioner in the land LAC No.110/16 Sh. Preetpal Singh Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 11 of 14 is 1/3rd and the share of the Sh. Raghubir Singh is 1/3rd.

sentences.text: That the share of Sh. Jawand Singh and Sh. Harcharan Singh in the land was paid to the petitioner in proceeding under Section 30-31 of the L.A. Act in respect of the same very land as per Order of the Court dated 19.07.2007 in LAC No.17/2007.

As such the share of the petitioner in the land comes to 2/3rd i.e. 1/3rd share of Sh. Jawand Singh and Sh. Harcharan Singh and 1/3rd share of the petitioner and the petitioner has got compensation in respect of the land to the extent of 2/3rd share in the reference petition under Section 30-31 of the L.A. Act and relied upon Ex.PW7/1.

However, on perusal of Ex.PW7/1, it is observed that it is the copy of order-sheet passed in LAC No.17/2007 dated 19.07.2007 and does not record any findings to the entitlement of the compensation of the petitioner herein in respect of land in question.
c) Further, during the course of submissions, it is argued by ld.

sentences.text: Upon perusal of the same, it is observed that the claim of petitioner on account of acquisition of land of Shop No.1/1142B and 1/1143 (First Floor), situated in Village Chandrawali, Shahdara was declined on the ground that petitioner is not having any right, title or interest in the land beneath the shop in question.

Further,
compensation for the structure has already been granted to him.
The said judgment has attained finality as not challenged by either party till date, as per record.
The relevant para of the judgment is reproduced herein:-

"In view of my findings on issue no.1, IP no.546 is not entitled to compensation for land in respect of property bearing no. 1/1142B and 1/1143 (First Floor), main road,
Makki Sarai, Shahdara".
e) Therefore, since in respect of the land in question i.e. Shop No.1/1142B and 1/1143, situated in Village Chandrawali, Shahdara, the compensation for the entire land has already been awarded to Sh. Jawand Singh i.e. father of the petitioner herein and

considering the fact that his claim has been specifically denied in the reference petition U/s 30-31, L.A. Act by the Court, he is not entitled to any compensation on account of acquisition of land in question.

Despite being aware of the findings recorded in reference petitions U/s 30-31, L.A. Act bearing LAC Nos.17/2007 and 15/2007, the petitioner, under the garb of shop constructed on First Floor on the same land is again claiming compensation of the land which has already been awarded to his father, who owned the land as per judgment dated 15.09.2007.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Sardar Jawand sold the First Floor of the property to the petitioner vide Power of Attorney, receipt, Will dt. 01.04.1993.
Thereafter, various interested persons including the petitioner had filed their objections and claims before the concerned SDM and he was to held an inquiry in respect of amount of compensation.
The petitioner also filed his claim along-with objections and all relevant records.
The petitioner along-with other interested persons had also filed an application U/s 11, L.A. Act for fixing the date for inquiry.
However, petitioner was never called for any inquiry and he was never given an opportunity to produce evidence in support of his claim.
The period of announcing the award was expiring due to which SDM, Karawal Nagar announced the award on 20.07.1999 without conducting any inquiry.
The award has not been served upon the petitioner till LAC No.110/16 Sh. Preetpal Singh Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 3 of 14 date, therefore,
the present reference petition is within the prescribed period of limitation.
The compensation assessed by LAC is sufficient and reasonable and it reflects the true market value prevailing at the time of notification issued U/s 4 of Act.
The petitioners have claimed excessive and exorbitant market value of the land and structures.
The LAC has considered the market value of the land on the date of publication of notification U/s 4 of Act i.e. 12.06.1997.
The Slum Area Improvement and Clearance Act is applicable to the land in dispute.
Petitioners are not entitled for enhanced compensation on the land in question.
The share of the petitioner in the land LAC No.110/16 Sh. Preetpal Singh Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 11 of 14 is 1/3rd and the share of the Sh. Raghubir Singh is 1/3rd.
That the share of Sh. Jawand Singh and Sh. Harcharan Singh in the land was paid to the petitioner in proceeding under Section 30-31 of the L.A. Act in respect of the same very land as per Order of the Court dated 19.07.2007 in LAC No.17/2007.

If so, at what rate?

As such the share of the petitioner in the land comes to 2/3rd i.e. 1/3rd share of Sh. Jawand Singh and Sh. Harcharan Singh and 1/3rd share of the petitioner and the petitioner has got compensation in respect of the land to the extent of 2/3rd share in the reference petition under Section 30-31 of the L.A. Act and relied upon Ex.PW7/1.

"In view of my findings on issue no.1, IP no.546 is not entitled to compensation for land in respect of property bearing no. 1/1142B and 1/1143 (First Floor), main road,
Makki Sarai, Shahdara".
e) Therefore, since in respect of the land in question i.e. Shop No.1/1142B and 1/1143, situated in Village Chandrawali, Shahdara, the compensation for the entire land has already been awarded to Sh. Jawand Singh i.e. father of the petitioner herein and
considering the fact that his claim has been specifically denied in the reference petition U/s 30-31, L.A. Act by the Court, he is not entitled to any compensation on account of acquisition of land in question.
Despite being aware of the findings recorded in reference petitions U/s 30-31, L.A. Act bearing LAC Nos.17/2007 and 15/2007, the petitioner, under the garb of shop constructed on First Floor on the same land is again claiming compensation of the land which has already been awarded to his father, who owned the land as per judgment dated 15.09.2007.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, this issue is decided against the petitioner.
a) In view of the findings recorded in the issue no.1, the petitioner is held not entitled to any compensation in respect of acquisition of the land in question i.e. Shop No.1/1142B and 1/1143 (First Floor), situated in Village Chandrawali, Shahdara.
However, the respondents are at liberty to seek recovery of compensation, if any, paid to the petitioner herein on account of acquisition of land in question i.e. Shop No.1/1142B and 1/1143 (First Floor), situated in Village Chandrawali, Shahdara as per the law.
The reference petition stands answered accordingly.
Both the parties shall bear their own costs.

No order as to cost.
